recipe.title: Dump-and-Go Crockpot Beef and Broccoli
recipe.summary: Tender slow-cooked lean beef with broccoli, a savory garlic-ginger sauce, and a modest portion of rice for approximately 42 grams of protein and 375 calories.
recipe.story: There is no browning or skillet work before leaving the house. The beef cooks directly in the sauce, while the broccoli and quick rice wait until evening so they stay fresh instead of turning to mush.
ingredients: 32 ounces raw lean top sirloin, sliced thinly against the grain
instructions: In the morning, place the sliced raw beef in a 6-quart slow cooker.
Add the beef bone broth, soy sauce, sweetener, rice vinegar, sesame oil, minced garlic, ground ginger, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours, until the beef is tender.
At night, whisk the cornstarch and cold water together until smooth. Stir the slurry into the slow cooker.
Add the broccoli florets, cover, and cook on HIGH for 20 to 30 minutes, until the broccoli is crisp-tender and the sauce has thickened.
Prepare or reheat 1 1/2 cups of cooked rice while the broccoli finishes.
Divide the rice and beef-and-broccoli mixture evenly among 6 bowls.
tips: Ask the butcher for thinly sliced top sirloin or slice it the night before to keep morning preparation truly dump-and-go.
Do not add the broccoli in the morning. Eight hours of cooking will make it very soft.
Use a zero-calorie brown-sugar-style sweetener to keep the meal below 400 calories.
Measure the finished rice carefully because extra rice changes the calories quickly.
Nutrition is approximate and varies by beef leanness and product brands.
